issues.legal_issue: A grant of the right to catch fish in a tank is a benefit arising out of land and is an immovable-property instrument subject to stamp duty.
material_facts: The appellants had been granted the right to catch fish in a tank.

The dispute proceeded on the premise that the grants were leases because the appellants did not contest that premise before the Division Bench and did not provide the instruments to the Supreme Court.
The Court treated the fishing right as a profit à prendre and a benefit arising out of land.
issues.conclusion: The grants were instruments subject to the applicable stamp duty, whether or not their terms required compulsory registration.
issues.legal_principle: The definition of immovable property in Section 2(18) of the Madhya Pradesh General Clauses Act includes benefits arising out of land. The right to catch fish is such a benefit and is a profit à prendre. Under Section 2(16) of the Indian Stamp Act, a lease includes specified written undertakings concerning immovable property, and the grant is an instrument chargeable under Article 35(a) of Schedule 1-A. In The Bihar Eastern Gangetic Fishermen Cooperative Society Ltd. v. Sipahi Singh, the Court held that a grant of a profit à prendre requires a registered instrument under the applicable property-transfer rules, whether the right is tangible or intangible. The other cited decisions concerning whether particular fishing grants were licences or leases were distinguished because their instruments and language were not before the Court here.

predicates.appeal_concerning_fishing_right_grant: The matter is an appeal concerning an instrument granting a right to catch fish.
predicates.fishing_right_benefits_land: The granted fishing right is exercised in a tank and provides a benefit arising from the land.
predicates.grant_treated_as_lease: The grant is treated as a lease for deciding the dispute.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a grant of a fishing right that benefits land and is treated as a lease, the grant instrument requires stamp duty.

issues.legal_issue: A lease for a term shorter than one year is not compulsorily registrable on the basis of its term alone.
material_facts: One fishing-right grant was treated as a lease with a term of nine months.
The Court proceeded on the premise that it was a lease because the lease-or-licence issue had not been raised before the Division Bench and the instrument was not produced before the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The nine-month lease was not compulsorily registrable, although it remained subject to stamp duty.
issues.legal_principle: Section 17(1)(c) of the Registration Act requires registration of leases of immovable property from year to year, for a term exceeding one year, or reserving a yearly rent. The Court held that the nine-month lease was not compulsorily registrable under that provision. The obligation to pay stamp duty is distinct from compulsory registration.

predicates.grant_treated_as_lease: The grant is treated as a lease for deciding the dispute.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns registration of a grant treated as a lease and its term is shorter than one year, the lease is not compulsorily registrable.

issues.legal_issue: A lease of immovable property for a term exceeding one year is compulsorily registrable.
material_facts: One fishing-right grant was treated as a lease for a term exceeding one year.
The Court proceeded on the premise that it was a lease because the lease-or-licence issue had not been raised before the Division Bench and the instrument was not produced before the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The lease for more than one year was compulsorily registrable and could not be acted upon unless duly stamped and registered.
issues.legal_principle: Section 17(1)(c) of the Registration Act requires registration of leases of immovable property from year to year, for a term exceeding one year, or reserving a yearly rent. The grant of the fishing right was also an instrument subject to stamp duty under the Indian Stamp Act.

predicates.lease_term_exceeds_one_year: The lease term is longer than one year.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns registration of a grant treated as a lease and its term exceeds one year, the lease is compulsorily registrable.
